title: superclaude-per-instance-memory-max
intention: A per-instance env var (CAIRN_SUPERCLAUDE_MEMORY_MAX_PER_INSTANCE) that sets the systemd scope memory ceiling for a specific superclaude instance.
why: The global SUPERCLAUDE_MEM_MAX cap is built, but per-instance tunability is not — a single instance that needs a different ceiling has no knob.
traces_to: Telos 2 (allow Akien to build tools that help) and Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics)

falsifier.proves_red: Set CAIRN_SUPERCLAUDE_MEMORY_MAX_PER_INSTANCE, launch superclaude, ask the kernel for the cgroup memory.max, verify it matches the per-instance value and not the global default.

how: The superclaude launcher already reads SUPERCLAUDE_MEM_MAX as a global default (line 490). Add a per-instance override: when instance N launches, check CAIRN_SUPERCLAUDE_MEMORY_MAX_PER_INSTANCE before falling back to SUPERCLAUDE_MEM_MAX. One env var, read at launch time, fed to the existing systemd-run scope's MemoryMax property.
watchme: none, because the proof at launchers/proofs/test_superclaude_memory_scope.py already verifies the kernel limit
what: A CAIRN_SUPERCLAUDE_MEMORY_MAX_PER_INSTANCE environment variable that sets the systemd scope memory ceiling for a specific superclaude instance, so we can just set it if we need to.

gates_bound.proof_gate: tester runs test_superclaude_memory_scope.py extended with a per-instance arm
